text:
alex.s: FYI forwarded an email from an engineer — subject 'Urgent: Rotate KMS key now' with a link to a 'rotation console'. looks phishy, attaching headers.
priya.r: can you paste the headers + the link? we'll block domain if it's malicious.
alex.s: From: hr-payments@redwood-secure[.]com
Reply-To: support-rotate@secure-rotations[.]net
Link: https://secure-rotations[.]net/rotate?k=abc123
No attachments, just a form that asks for service-account JSON and our KMS key ARN.
jamie.k: ugh. asks for service account JSON + KMS ARN — classic credential harvesting. did anyone actually submit anything?
alex.s: user says they clicked the link but didn't upload anything. they entered their email and org, then closed it. no creds pasted.
mike.ops: good. immediate asks: 1) check KMS audit logs for any Decrypt/Encrypt/GenerateDataKey events for our customer-master keys in the last 24h 2) check IAM for any new keys/grants 3) block the domain and add to phishing corpus.
chris.m: running quick query against cloud logs now:
```
# GCP
gcloud logging read "resource.type=project AND protoPayload.methodName=(\"google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt\" OR \"Encrypt\")" --freshness=24h --project=redwood-prod
```
chris.m: result: zero Decrypt calls for our CMKs in the timeframe. no unexpected service account activity in IAM audit logs either.
priya.r: AWS side check?
chris.m: AWS CloudTrail query:
```
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=GenerateDataKey --start-time 2024-06-01T00:00:00Z --end-time 2024-06-02T00:00:00Z
```
chris.m: nothing. no GenerateDataKey or CreateGrant events for our KMS keys.
jamie.k: ok status = no signs of KMS access. still rotate any service-account keys the user had access to, and rotate/rotate-schedule the keys that were referenced in the email (defense-in-depth).
sec-bot: incident created INC-2024-9107 by priya.r (phishing: attempted KMS credential harvest). severity: medium. responders: eng-security, infra-ops.
priya.r: can infra rotate the service account keys and rotate our customer-facing KMS rotation schedule for sensitive keys? mike? chris?
mike.ops: i'll rotate the service account keys that the reporter had access to and create new creds. will also add a targeted CI job to invalidate any short-lived tokens issued last 48h.
chris.m: posted domain to security blockade list and added to Mimecast quarantine. added sample to sandbox. sandbox result: landing page attempts to POST to https://collector.secure-rotations[.]net/api/submit and returns 302 -> downloads a tiny JS that exfiltrates form fields. payload tried to contact 3 IPs (tor exit + two cloud provider VMs). blocked.
priya.r: good. next: update audit log retention pointer and run a deeper retrospective for last 7 days for any lateral activity. also request an emergency KMS policy review — ensure no overly permissive grants.
jamie.k: I'll draft a comms blurb to staff: short advisory not to click rotation links, how to verify, and how to forward suspicious email to phishing@redwood.com. include screenshots.
alex.s: can we include a brief how-to: if you get an email asking for key material, always verify via the console or internal ticket, never via a 3rd-party link.
priya.r: agreed. action items: 1) mike rotate keys and invalidate tokens (done by EOD) 2) chris deep log review (24h) 3) jamie comms + training reminder (tomorrow) 4) add IOC to SIEM and blocklist (immediate).
sec-bot: incident status updated INC-2024-9107 -> containment in progress. updated responders.
mike.ops: keys rotated, tokens revoked. posted PR to infra runbook with emergency rotation steps: https://go/redwood/runbooks/km-rotations
jamie.k: comms ready draft: "Heads up — phishing campaign impersonating 'Redwood Secure' asking to rotate KMS keys via a 3rd-party link. Do not click. If you clicked, don't paste secrets, report to security." will send once priya approves.
priya.r: approved. send company-wide at 11:30. file post-incident checklist and mark root cause as credential-harvest via typosquat domain. follow-up: schedule a short all-engineers training on verifying key rotation requests next week.
alex.s: thanks team. closing thread, will add final incident notes when chris finishes deep review.
